questions.def: "Must" is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He must ___ very tired after the long trip.

questions.def: "Can't" is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: She can't ___ at work yet. It's only 7 AM.

questions.def: "Must" is followed directly by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He must to go to the store.

questions.def: "Must" indicates a strong deduction based on evidence.
questions.question: She ___ be at home. I saw her car there.

questions.def: "Might" is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: They might ___ to the party, but I'm not sure.

questions.def: "Could well" indicates a possibility.
questions.question: He could ___ be right, but I doubt it.

questions.def: "May be" is followed by a present participle or adjective, not a base verb.
questions.question: She may be arrive late.

questions.def: "Must" indicates a strong belief based on evidence.
questions.question: It ___ be him. He's the only one who knows.

questions.def: "Can't have" indicates a past deduction that is impossible.
questions.question: It can't ___ rained. The ground is dry.

questions.def: "Might have" indicates a past possibility.
questions.question: He might ___ forgotten his keys.

questions.def: "Should have" is followed by the past participle.
questions.question: She should had gone to the doctor.

questions.def: "Must have" indicates a strong past deduction.
questions.question: They ___ have gone to the beach. It's sunny.

questions.def: "Couldn't have" indicates a past deduction that is impossible.
questions.question: She couldn't ___ seen him. He was abroad.

questions.def: "May have" indicates a past possibility.
questions.question: He may ___ arrived late. The traffic was bad.

questions.def: "Might have" does not need "to".
questions.question: They might to have left already.

questions.def: "Must have been" indicates a strong past deduction.
questions.question: He ___ have been tired. He worked all night.

questions.def: "Can't have" indicates something is unlikely.
questions.question: She can't ___ that much money.

questions.def: "Should have" indicates regret or criticism.
questions.question: He should ___ called, but he didn't.

questions.def: "May" is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: She may to go soon.

questions.def: "Must" indicates a strong deduction based on evidence.
questions.question: It ___ be cold outside. I see frost.

questions.def: "Could well" expresses a strong possibility.
questions.question: He could ___ be at home. He said he would be.

questions.def: "Must be" expresses a logical deduction.
questions.question: They must ___ tired. They worked all day.

questions.def: "Can't" is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: She can't to speak Spanish.

questions.def: "Must have" expresses a strong past deduction or surprise.
questions.question: He ___ have eaten all the cake!

questions.def: "Might not" expresses a possibility that something will not happen.
questions.question: It might ___ rain later. Take an umbrella.

questions.def: "Couldn't have" expresses impossibility in the past.
questions.question: She couldn't ___ known about the surprise.

questions.def: "Should" is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He should to study more.

questions.def: "May have" indicates a past possibility.
questions.question: I ___ have seen her at the party.

questions.def: "Might have" suggests a possibility.
questions.question: She ___ have gone to the wrong house.

questions.def: "Can't possibly" expresses strong disbelief.
questions.question: He can't ___ be serious!
